PullRequest.Title: Agents - improve changeset picker layout + hover
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request reverts the recent changes made to the changeset picker in the agents window, specifically addressing user feedback regarding the border and hover text. 

Changes include:
- Removed the border from the changeset picker while preserving high-contrast accessibility borders and keyboard-focus styling.
- Eliminated the "Versions: " prefix from the picker’s hover text and updated the related accessibility label.
- Updated the hover text for "Branch Changes" to display the branch comparison description (e.g., `feature -> main`) instead of the static label, while keeping the visible label unchanged.

All relevant tests have been updated and passed successfully.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering and updating the selected changeset picker in the Changes editor header or Changes view files header
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing observable autorun reads the selected changeset, updates the in-place label, managed-hover content, ARIA label, and availability synchronously. The diff adds only a read of the already-materialized optional description and chooses it for tooltip text; no asynchronous work must complete.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active changeset per picker update. The catalogue is scanned once by the unchanged default-changeset logic; the new description selection is O(1), independent of file count and changeset count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-thread updates are serialized by the observable autorun. There is no spawned concurrency, queue, limiter, or fan-out introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing derived observable cache retains the prior label while a replacement catalogue is loading. The tooltip string is stored in the same cached value and follows the same invalidation; no new cache, miss path, negative cache, or unbounded key set is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the constructor, autorun, tooltip base class, and changeset provider show the description is precomputed and no filesystem, IPC, network, subprocess, database, or serialization boundary is reached.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact picker update frequency varies with session and summary changes, but each changed operation is a bounded property read/string choice on an existing update path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff does not increase update cardinality, reconstruct DOM, add layout reads, or introduce expensive boundary work; tooltip localization already occurred on summary updates before the change.

Scenarios.Scenario: Painting the picker across normal, high-contrast, hover, and keyboard-focus states
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CSS style resolution and paint occur on the existing picker element. The normal-theme border declaration is removed, while the existing high-contrast selector now supplies the full border declaration; no script, layout read, or nested relayout is added.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A constant number of picker elements, rather than rows or files; cost does not grow with repository size or session history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser style/layout/paint work remains on the normal rendering pipeline with no changed scheduling or concurrent task creation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache participates. Browser style caching behavior is not materially changed by replacing one constant declaration with another theme-scoped declaration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete CSS hunks and surrounding selectors show no filters, geometry queries, animations, or DOM expansion.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser-specific paint details are not measured, but the changed declarations are constant-size and affect only the picker element.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change removes normal-theme border paint and preserves a constant-cost high-contrast border without adding scaling rendering work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and traced both picker instances, their observable update path, tooltip/ARIA handling, the branch-description producer, and CSS paint scope. No diff-introduced performance issue or concrete regression fix was found.
